frontier.hypothesis: F19 - the whole remaining 7 is one scheduling decision: target issues lw a3,0(a0) as the LAST memory reference of the argument block, we issue it at build idx 54.
frontier.mechanism: Target keeps the idx[0] address chain alive in $a0 across the third argument's entire computation; ours runs that chain through $v0 and loads a3 early, which drags the arg5 chain later and produces all 7 diffs. H39 measured twelve argument spellings and 7 is the floor of that family; session 6 separately showed source statement placement inside this block is byte-inert because rank_for_schedule decides on INSN_PRIORITY and the dependence-class test (sched.c:2412-2449) and never reaches the INSN_LUID tie-break (sched.c:2452-2455). So the lever is not in the C's statement order or argument spelling.
frontier.next_probe: Read the priorities instead of guessing spellings. Run `bash tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s9/idump.sh t3` and compare each argument-block insn's INSN_PRIORITY and dependence list in the `;; Function saEft01Init` section of system.i.sched against the order target emits. The specific question is what makes target's lw a3 the LOWEST-priority insn in the block when it is the last link of the shortest of the three chains; a likely answer is an anti-dependence on $a0 from the following `lui a0,%hi(D_800161C8)`, in which case the lever is which pseudo local_alloc gives $a0 (a copy-preference question) rather than anything in the C.
